triage.if_false: The alert is false if each flagged event has exactly one ledger posting and the gap disappears when the money check is rerun once the provider's records have settled. findings.cause: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 2026-11-18T01:00:37Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. From then on it posts every Kafka message it receives and does not check whether the provider event id was already booked. The provider resends each webhook until it is acknowledged, and webhook-receiver publishes every resend as a new message on provider-events. So the same event reaches ledger-consumer at several offsets, and each copy is posted. This breaks posted_exactly_once for 7 events. Each extra posting also moves provider_clearing away from the provider's balance, which breaks matches_provider. The extra postings are 6 payment.succeeded events posted twice, one of them (evt_000308, $131.93) posted three times, and one refund posted twice. diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, and Kafka lag builds briefly on provider-events. Payments, refunds and payment-confirmer are untouched. If the earlier settings were not a deduplicating handler, duplicates continue; c2 does not show what the earlier settings were. Messages consumed during the switchover are deduplicated only if the restored handler checks event ids against the ledger. The rollback does not remove the existing $493.23 of extra postings: those need a separate, reviewed data repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter) on image sha256:e19dccfc9399. This is not advisable, because those settings cause the duplicates. More practically, if the restored handler misbehaves (errors, a stalled consumer group), stop ledger-consumer so that it posts nothing. Its consumer-group offsets keep the backlog in Kafka until a correct handler is running.
